summary:
I ported the four owned modules that have Windows-relevant behaviour. The other nine owned modules needed no edits, as the app spec says. Nobody had edited these files before me: 'git diff HEAD --stat' was empty for all 13, so I started from HEAD.

Changes:
(1) runtime_version.source_digest now follows C spec 5.7 and spec §11. It uses os.scandir and keeps only regular files whose name ends with the exact lowercase '.py'. Names are sorted by their UTF-8 bytes, not by a case-insensitive Windows glob or WindowsPath order. Files are read with _platform.read_bytes_shared, a reader that lets other processes replace or delete the file at the same time, so an update is not blocked. The hashed byte stream (name, NUL, bytes, NUL) is unchanged.
(2) schema.py: station time zones are now validated with _platform.canonical_timezone, which only accepts the exact-case IANA key. Windows file lookups ignore case and trailing dots or spaces, so 'europe/istanbul' would otherwise be stored. The error is still StoreError('unknown IANA station timezone'). The import_profiles validator now calls validate_import_config(..., persisted=True).
(3) settings.py: new import profiles must use Windows absolute allowed_roots (drive or UNC, no NUL), checked with _platform.stored_path_flavour/is_absolute. Profiles stored on Linux with POSIX roots ('/srv/music') still pass the schema validator, so integrity checks, factory-reset retirement and transfer packages keep working. import_options() and new saves reject them with the Turkish message 'İçe aktarım profili Linux klasör yolları içeriyor; Windows klasörlerini yeniden seçin.' A transfer-package import of such a profile is now skipped with that message as its warning.
(4) desktop_broadcast.py: a newly saved broadcast_record filename must also pass _platform.component_valid, which rejects names like 'kayıt:1.wav', 'CON.wav', 'a*b.wav', 'a?.wav' and '"x".wav'. Stored documents (persisted=True) are still accepted.

clocks.py, plans.py and the schema.py offline-grant check only compute with ZoneInfo on keys that were already validated, so the bundled tzdata is enough. broadcast_services, desktop_autodj, desktop_copyright, desktop_playlist, endpoint_protocol, playback_markers and readiness contain only pure logic: no OS calls, no path rules, no platform-dependent time formatting. None of the 13 files had fcntl, pwd, grp, signal, /proc, os.open, subprocess, chmod or POSIX path code, so nothing Linux-specific was left to remove.
api:
Changed public signatures:
- settings.validate_import_config(value, *, persisted: bool = False) -> dict. persisted=True also accepts stored POSIX ('legacy-posix') allowed_roots; the default (new saves) requires Windows absolute roots without NUL.
- settings.LINUX_ROOTS_MESSAGE is a new constant with the Turkish message. settings.import_options raises StoreError(LINUX_ROOTS_MESSAGE) when a stored profile has non-Windows roots.

Unchanged signatures, new behaviour:
- runtime_version.source_digest() -> str. Selects exact lowercase '.py' regular files, sorts by the UTF-8 bytes of the name, and hashes name\0bytes\0 for each file.
- desktop_broadcast.validate_configuration(kind, config, sid, state, *, persisted=False): for broadcast_record when persisted=False, the filename must also pass _platform.component_valid.
- schema station validation: _platform.canonical_timezone.

All other modules keep their public API unchanged.
verification: Imported all 13 owned modules once with the Windows CPython 3.14.8 under wrun ('wrun /home/user/RadioSs/runtime/python/python.exe -E -s -B -X utf8 -c ...', cwd=database/SDBASE/src): every import printed OK. That process also called source_digest() (it returned a hex digest) and ran a few validator calls; their output matched the intended behaviour for the four changes, see the summary.
Checked that the four changed files are still pure LF (0 CR bytes) and UTF-8, which matters for the source digest (D13).

As instructed for this fast write-only pass, I did not run any tests (including tests/test_desktop_broadcast.py), start a service, or exercise the HTTP API or the stop event. The user verifies on their Windows PC.
industrial_fixes: settings.validate_import_config: an allowed_roots entry containing NUL was accepted and later crashed Path(root).resolve() in rekordbox.map_media_path / media._validate_source with ValueError (HTTP 500). It is now rejected as StoreError when saved.

settings.import_options: a profile stored on Linux with POSIX roots would have been used on Windows as rooted-relative paths ('\\srv\\music' on the current drive) and silently matched nothing. It now fails closed with a clear Turkish message, and the stored row stays valid for integrity checks and reset.

schema.py: station time zones are validated with the exact-case key, so non-canonical keys ('europe/istanbul', 'Europe/Istanbul ') can no longer be stored; the C side and other tools would reject them.

desktop_broadcast.py: recording filenames that are invalid on NTFS (':' would create an alternate data stream, device names, wildcard characters) can no longer be saved, so the C recorder can no longer fail on every take with such a name.

runtime_version.source_digest: the digest no longer depends on case-insensitive Windows glob or sort order, which could make the service disagree with the C client and tools and cause endless 'stale service' restarts. Reads also no longer block an updater replacing a module (sharing violation).
requests_for_other_areas: tools area (tools/radios_database_setup.py:185-198, backend_source_digest): use the same selection and order as sdbase/runtime_version.source_digest. That means os.scandir with name.endswith('.py') (exact lowercase), regular files only, and sorted by name.encode('utf-8'), not sorted(package.glob('*.py')). The current version sorts WindowsPath objects case-insensitively and globs case-insensitively.

C area (src/core/data_client.c:896-917, installed_source_digest): the strcmp order and exact '.py' suffix already match. It should also skip non-regular entries (directories or links named '*.py'), as the Python side and spec §11 do (is_file(follow_symlinks=False)). Today such an entry would make the C digest fail or differ.

tests area: tests/test_desktop_broadcast.py:113 — add the Windows-invalid record names from spec §6.9 ('kayıt:1.wav', 'CON.wav', 'a*b.wav', 'a?.wav', '"x".wav') to the invalid variants list. Add tests for settings: a new profile with '/srv/music' raises StoreError; a stored Linux profile survives a reset retire and integrity check; import_options raises the Turkish message; 'D:\\Müzik' and '\\\\srv\\share' are accepted. Add a schema test that 'europe/istanbul' and 'Europe/Istanbul ' are rejected for stations.
open_issues: No tests were run (user decision). Untested: the existing tests that touch these modules (test_desktop_broadcast, test_desktop_transfer_package, test_desktop_reset, and the clock/plan/readiness tests).

source_digest now skips a symlink or directory named '*.py' in the package. The C client (data_client.c) currently still includes any name ending in '.py', so the two only agree once the C request above is done. In a normal checkout no such entries exist.

A profile created on Linux with POSIX allowed_roots cannot be used until it is re-saved with Windows folders (intended fail-closed behaviour from spec §6.10). A transfer-package import skips such profiles with a warning instead of importing them disabled.
